title: This CPI Report is Bad for MANY Reasons...
speaker: Kevin Paffrath

macro_themes.view: Core CPI ~0.35% m/m, a right-tail miss; half of categories above 3% y/y, which Warsh says means more hikes.
Market now prices ~3.86 more hikes to Sept 2027 and ~50% odds of an October hike.
Real worker pricing power falling 0.7% y/y; layoffs will eventually push unemployment sharply higher.
Only an Iran deal (ideally Oct 20-27) can calm the 10-year; otherwise Fed hikes in October and December.

calls.condition: Yields stay elevated unless an Iran deal arrives
calls.reason: Hot CPI and supercore at 0.42% keep the 10-year rubber-banding above 5.27; only an Iran deal brings relief.
calls.quote: we have still rubber banded above that 5.27. Now, I hope this fades today because 5.312 is high

calls.reason: Peak fear (QQQ ~700) is behind; still optimistic, but this is not a dip worth buying.
calls.quote: I remain optimistic... this isn't the level where I want to buy the dip because it's not much of a dip

calls.reason: Cash-rich companies outperform as rates rise; highly indebted names like CoreWeave do worse.
calls.quote: as usual, the cash-rich companies are doing the best. That's Apple

notes: No explicit date or session time; recorded shortly after CPI release. AAPL is an implied relative-strength view, not an explicit trade.
